preconditions.expression: all(line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip())
preconditions.description: Every line in stdin is non-empty and represents either a test case count, grid dimensions, or grid row.
The first line of stdin is a positive integer T (number of test cases).

preconditions.expression: all(len(line) == M for line in grid_lines) and all(c in {'.', '#'} for line in grid_lines for c in line)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the grid has exactly M columns per row, and each cell is either '.' (empty) or '#' (wall). Here, grid_lines is the list of N lines for the current test case, and M is the number of columns.
The starting cell (1, 1) is always empty ('.'). Here, grid_lines is the list of N lines for the current test case.

preconditions.expression: N >= 1 and M >= 1 and N * M >= 2
preconditions.description: For each test case, N (rows) and M (columns) are positive integers with N*M >= 2.

postconditions.expression: all(len(output_line) == 1 and output_line.isdigit() for output_line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is a single line containing a non-negative integer representing the minimum number of airstrikes required.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(output_line) <= N for output_line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: The output for each test case is a non-negative integer not exceeding the number of rows N.

postconditions.expression: all(min_airstrikes == min_k where k in range(0, N+1) and exists_path_after_airstrikes(grid_lines, k))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output integer min_airstrikes is the smallest k such that there exists a path from (1, 1) to (N, M) after removing all walls in any k rows. Here, exists_path_after_airstrikes(grid_lines, k) is true if, after removing all walls in any k rows, there is a path from (1, 1) to (N, M) using only adjacent cells (up, down, left, right) without walls.
